clues.title: Driving side: left
text: South Africa drives on the **left.**
NOTE: A handful of other countries also drive on the left. See [this](/images/south-africa/rightleftdrive.png) infographic for more information.

images.caption: Traffic driving on the left, with a two-way traffic warning sign

clues.summary: Traffic drives on the left. A handful of other countries do too.

clues.title: Road lines: yellow edges, white centre
text: On most roads, South Africa utilizes single **yellow outer lines **and white centre lines.
NOTE: The other southern African countries of Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho and Namibia also use single yellow outer lines.
!!Australia practically never uses yellow outer lines.
clues.summary: Single yellow lines at the road edge and white lines in the middle. Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho and Namibia use them too. Australia practically never uses yellow edge lines.

differs.how: Practically never has yellow edge lines

clues.title: Road lines: white triple centre line
text: South Africa occasionally features unique white **triple centre lines** with 2 solid lines on the outside and a dashed line on the inside.
You may also sometimes encounter another unique triple centre line, consisting of two white lines with one yellow line in the middle. These centre lines are usually found on larger main roads.
NOTE: The only other countries where you will find road lines like these are the other southern African countries of Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho and Namibia.
clues.summary: Sometimes a triple centre line: two solid white lines with a dashed one inside. Another version has two white lines with a yellow one in the middle, usually on big main roads. Only the neighbouring southern African countries have these.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 2, big round blur, sky halo
text: **Generation 2 coverage** is quite common in the country.
It can be recognized by the large circular car blur and the halo-like colour distortion in the sky.
NOTE: On the continent of Africa, Generation 2 is only found in South Africa.
clues.summary: Gen 2 is fairly common. It has a big round blur where the car is and a halo-like colour glow in the sky. In Africa, only this country has Gen 2.

clues.title: Language: English plus Afrikaans place names
text: South Africa has **11 official languages**: English, Afrikaans, and various Bantu languages. English is the [lingua franca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingua_franca) and therefore appears most often on signage.

**Afrikaans** is a Germanic language that is closely related to Dutch. Common Afrikaans place name suffixes are -fontein, -kraal, -kop, -dorp, -nek, and -berg or -burg. While Afrikaans is most commonly spoken in the [western half](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/South_Africa_2011_Afrikaans_speakers_proportion_map.svg/2337px-South_Africa_2011_Afrikaans_speakers_proportion_map.svg.png) of the country, you will find Afrikaans place names all over South Africa, meaning that it is not useful for region-guessing.
NOTE: Afrikaans is rare to non-existent in Eswatini and Lesotho. It is also abundantly rare in Botswana, but has some limited presence in the form of place names.

images.caption: Welcome sign in Afrikaans, Xhosa and English with a regional coat of arms

clues.summary: English is most common on signs. Afrikaans looks like Dutch, with place name endings like -fontein, -kraal, -kop, -dorp, -nek and -berg. It appears nationwide, so it does not help pick a region.

clues.title: Pole: bird poles, white insulators on bars
text: The most common type of pole in South Africa features 1 to 5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators that resemble rows of birds, which is why they are referred to as “**bird poles**” in the community.
NOTE: South Africa has a wide variety of other poles and pole tops. Some of these are (mostly) limited to a certain region; you can learn more about them in the region guessing section.
clues.summary: The most common pole has 1 to 5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators that look like rows of birds. Many other pole types exist, some limited to certain regions.

clues.title: Sign: green direction sign, yellow road number
text: South Africa uses **green** directional signs with the road number in yellow.
NOTE: Green directional signs with yellow road numbers are also used in Lesotho, Eswatini, Botswana and Namibia. Here, the format of road numbers is useful:
- !!N and R-roads are exclusive to South Africa.
- !!A and B-roads are exclusive to Botswana, Lesotho and Namibia. In addition to this, Namibia uses C, D, M and F roads.
- !!MR-roads are exclusive to Eswatini.
clues.summary: Green direction signs with a yellow road number. Neighbours use the same, so read the number: N and R roads exist only here, A and B roads in Botswana, Lesotho and Namibia, and MR roads in Eswatini.

clues.title: Sign: triangular warning sign, red border
text: South Africa utilizes **triangular warning signs** with a red border and a white background.
NOTE: The four other southern African countries use similar warning signs.
!!Australia and New Zealand use yellow diamond-shaped warning signs.
clues.summary: Warning signs are red-bordered triangles on white. The other southern African countries use similar ones. Australia and New Zealand use yellow diamonds.

clues.title: Chevron: white-and-red, plus thin single-arrow ones
text: South Africa uses **white-and-red **chevrons. You can find a similar chevron pattern below directional signs.
In addition, unique-looking [small, thin chevrons](https://goo.gl/maps/UtnQqFLqBe9EupxC6) with one arrow are common next to roads.
NOTE: The thin chevrons can also be found in the other southern African countries of Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho and Namibia.
clues.summary: White-and-red chevrons, with the same pattern under direction signs. Small thin single-arrow chevrons by the road are common, and neighbouring southern African countries have them too.

clues.title: Houses: high walls, fences and gates
text: Suburban houses in and around large cities will often be surrounded by **high walls,** fences, and gates** **to deter criminals.
clues.summary: Suburban houses in and around big cities are often surrounded by high walls, fences and gates.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 blue car, short antenna
text: All Generation 4 coverage in South Africa was taken by a blue Street View car with a short antenna.
NOTE: The antenna is sometimes [hidden by the blur](https://maps.app.goo.gl/fKdBXrspbEe8CeaF9).
clues.summary: All Gen 4 coverage shows a blue car with a short antenna. The blur sometimes hides the antenna.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 smallcam, low with big blur
text: South Africa also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, but with a short antenna on the back.

images.caption: Four panels labelled front panned down, front panned straight, back panned down and good blur (front)

clues.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than normal, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through, but a short antenna shows at the back.

clues.title: Plate: each province has its own design
text: Each province features a **different **licence plate design, which can be somewhat visible through the blur. Most notably Free State or KwaZulu-Natal, which have a slight green tint and blue tint respectively.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Plate designs differ by province and may show through the blur. Two stand out: one has a slight green tint, another a blue tint.

clues.title: Sign: N before the number, blue pentagon on maps
text: A map of major highways in South Africa. On road signs, the **letter ‘N’ **should appear in front of the highway number. On Google Maps, however, the letter ‘N’ will not be present. Instead, a **blue pentagon** with the number will be displayed.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: On road signs the highway number has an N in front. On Google Maps the N is missing and a blue pentagon with the number is shown instead.

clues.title: Sign: three-digit R roads grouped by region
text: Most of the **R-roads with three-digit road numbers** are geographically grouped. However, many roads go through multiple provinces and some, especially the 100s, are spread throughout the whole country. The map shows roughly where you can find each set of R-roads.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Most three-digit R roads are geographically grouped, but many cross provinces and the 100s are spread across the whole country. The map shows roughly where each set is.

clues.title: Phone numbers: 10 digits, area code starts with 0
text: **Telephone numbers** are 10 digits long. The first three digits of landline numbers are the area code. The first digit is always a zero; the second and third digits give you the area. The area codes are geographically grouped, so even learning just the first digit is useful.
NOTE: Mobile phone numbers start with 06–08. These numbers are not specific to an area.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
_Image provided by dbldk._
clues.summary: Numbers are 10 digits. Landlines start with a 0 followed by two digits for the area, and areas are geographically grouped. Mobile numbers start with 06 to 08 and say nothing about area.

clues.title: Pole: narrow A-shaped top on a horizontal bar
text: Poles with 3 bars forming the letter **‘A’**, with the bottom insulators being attached at the edges of a horizontal bar, can be found almost exclusively in Western Cape, and rarely in bordering provinces.
clues.summary: Poles with 3 bars forming an A, with the bottom insulators on the ends of a horizontal bar. Almost only in the south-west, rarely in neighbouring provinces.

clues.title: Pole: wide A-shaped top, insulators on the A
text: A similar poletop can be found in Eastern Cape, however the A-shape is noticeably wider and the bottom insulators are attached directly to the ‘A’ rather than a horizontal bar.
clues.summary: Similar A-shape but noticeably wider, with the bottom insulators attached directly to the A instead of a horizontal bar. Found in the south-east.

clues.title: Pole: trident pole tops
text: **Trident pole tops** are almost unique to KwaZulu-Natal.
clues.summary: Trident pole tops are almost unique to the east coast province.

clues.title: Pole: 3 alternating insulators sticking out sideways
text: Poles with **3 alternating insulators **sticking out horizontally at the top are mostly seen in the four northern provinces of Limpopo, Gauteng, North West and Mpumalanga. They can also sometimes be found in Northern Cape. In the rest of the country, these pole tops are exceedingly rare.
clues.summary: Poles with 3 alternating insulators sticking out horizontally are mostly in the four northern provinces, sometimes the north-west dry region. Very rare elsewhere.

clues.title: Pole: two diagonal bars forming a < shape
text: Poles with 2 **diagonal bars **forming a ‘<’ shape can be found mostly in the northeastern provinces, most commonly in Limpopo and North West.
clues.summary: Poles with 2 diagonal bars forming a < shape are mostly in the north-east, most often in the far north and the north-west.

clues.title: Pole: 1 or 2 metal arms holding insulators
text: Poles with **1 or 2 metal arms** holding up insulators are most commonly seen in Mpumalanga.

images.caption: Pole with metal arms holding insulators; red arrows point to the arms at the top

clues.summary: Poles with one or two metal arms are most common in the east, in one inland province.

clues.title: Sign: square red stickers on sign backs
text: **Square, red stickers **on the back of regular signs are often found in Eastern cape and close to Eastern cape in Northern Cape and Free State. You may see them in the North West province as well, but to a lesser extent.
NOTE: Red stickers on the back of chevrons can be seen in almost every province.

images.caption: Inset circle zooms in on a small red square sticker on the back of the sign

clues.summary: Square red stickers on the back of regular signs are common in the south-east and close to it in the dry north-west and the centre. A little in the north-west. Red stickers on chevron backs appear in almost every province.

clues.title: Sign: white stickers on chevron backs
text: **White stickers **on the back of chevrons are often seen in the Cape provinces.

images.caption: Red arrow points to the sticker on the back of the sign post

clues.summary: White stickers on the back of chevrons are often seen in the Cape provinces in the south and west.

clues.title: Road: grainy pavement with a pink tint
text: You can find this **grainy**, almost Texas-like pavement with a hint of **pink **in Limpopo.

images.caption: A grainy road surface with a pink tint

clues.summary: A grainy, almost Texas-like road surface with a hint of pink, found in the far north-east.

clues.title: Pole: big bird nests on top
text: Big **bird nests** on top of poles are commonly seen in the northern part of the Northern Cape Province.

images.caption: A huge bird nest on top of a pole in a dry landscape
A huge bird nest on top of a pole in a dry landscape

clues.summary: Big bird nests sit on top of poles, commonly in the northern part of the dry north-west province.

clues.title: Landscape: power plants between two towns
text: **Power plants** are often seen in between the town of Secunda and eMalahleni in Mpumalanga.

images.caption: Power plant cooling towers and chimneys between two towns

clues.summary: Power plants appear between two towns in the east inland province.

clues.title: Landscape: dry, barren, orange-red soil, shrub hills
text: The northeast of the country can look very dry and somewhat barren, with a lot of orange or red soil. You will often see hills or mountains covered in shrubs.
NOTE: Depending on the season, the coverage can change drastically from [dry](https://maps.app.goo.gl/XsQme5RXp7jB2U1p6) to [very green](https://maps.app.goo.gl/hLARbuFeBKWx6hot7).
clues.summary: The north-east can look very dry and barren, with orange or red soil and hills covered in shrubs. Coverage can change from dry to very green depending on season.

clues.title: Landscape: rocky treeless mountains, steep sides
text: Unique **rocky**, treeless mountains can be seen in Western Cape, with most of the mountains having tall, steep sides and sharp peaks.
NOTE: Similar mountains can be seen in and around Lesotho.
clues.summary: Rocky, treeless mountains with tall steep sides and sharp peaks in the south-west. Similar mountains are in and around Lesotho.

clues.title: Crops: vineyards in coastal valleys
text: Vineyards are almost exclusively found in** Western Cape**, mostly in valleys near the coast. You can also commonly find them near Upington, in Northern Cape.
clues.summary: Vineyards are almost only in the south-west, mostly in coastal valleys. They also appear near one inland town in the north-west.

clues.title: Landscape: dry land with red soil, north-west
text: A dry landscape with red soil is typically found in the Northern Cape.
NOTE: This [map](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c8/Koppen-Geiger_Map_ZAF_present.svg) is a useful guide in guessing based on the climate of South Africa.
clues.summary: A dry landscape with red soil is typical of the north-west province. The climate map is a useful guide.

clues.title: Crops: sugarcane along the east coast
text: **Sugarcane plantations** are most commonly seen in KwaZulu-Natal, mostly along the coast. However, they can also be seen in Mpumalanga on the Mozambique border. For an overview, see [this](/images/south-africa/southafrica_sugarcane.jpg) map.
clues.summary: Sugarcane plantations are most common on the east coast, and also on the north-east border in another province.

clues.title: Plants: very tall Cook pines on the south-east coast
text: Uniquely tall **Cook pine trees** are found mostly between the cities of East London and Durban along the southeastern coast.
NOTE: These are planted and not native, so they can be found anywhere along the coast.
clues.summary: Tall Cook pines grow mostly between two south-east coast cities. They are planted, so they can appear anywhere on the coast.

clues.title: Plants: pine plantations next to the western border
text: **Tree plantations** that consist mostly of pine** **are common to the west of Eswatini, and some to the south in KwaZulu-Natal.
NOTE: Pine tree plantations are typically seen within the country of Eswatini itself.

images.caption: Pine plantations along a winding road, with a red arrow and zoom circle on the pines at lower left

clues.summary: Tree plantations that are mostly pine are common west of Eswatini and in some parts of the east coast province to the south. Pine plantations are normally seen inside Eswatini itself.

clues.title: Landscape: grassy rolling hills, ridges north or east
text: **Grassy rolling hills** are generally located in the coastal area of Western Cape between Cape Town and George, and just north of Cape Town. Tall ridges are usually visible to the north or east.
clues.summary: Grassy rolling hills on the south-west coast between the main city and a southern town, and just north of the city. Tall ridges usually appear to the north or east.

clues.title: Landscape: flat and green subtropical near the border
text: The landscape near the Mozambique border in the highlighted area is noticeably **flat**, with green subtropical vegetation.
clues.summary: Near the north-east border with Mozambique the land is noticeably flat with green subtropical plants.

clues.title: Google car: camouflage car, black mirrors, roof racks
text: A **camouflage **car with black side mirrors and roof racks can be seen in Kruger National Park, on the Mozambique border.
NOTE: The Park now also has generation 4 coverage.

images.caption: Roof of a camouflage-pattern Google car with black mirrors at lower left

clues.summary: In the big north-east national park, a camouflage car with black side mirrors and roof racks. The park also has Gen 4 coverage now.

clues.title: Landscape: flat savannah, grass and small trees, waystones
text: The landscape around Kruger National Park is generally flat, with a **savannah **climate and dry vegetation. You will not see any agriculture and the vegetation is mostly made up of grasses, with small trees dotting the landscape. Red soil can also be seen below the grass.
In addition, this distinctive [directional waystone](https://goo.gl/maps/C4VRQ6v1PyAStJUz7) is commonly found at many junctions.
NOTE: Within the coverage of the park, you will mostly find unpaved gravel roads or small and paved roads without road lines.

images.caption: Flat savannah of grass and small trees in three views; the red circle zooms in on a roadside waystone.

clues.summary: Around the big north-east park: flat, dry savannah with grass, scattered small trees, red soil, and distinctive direction waystones at junctions. Mostly gravel roads or small unmarked paved roads.

clues.title: Sign: M route signs in two coastal cities
text: **Metropolitan Routes** are major roads around cities. They are designated with the letter M.
These distinct and unique M route signs are commonly found in [Port Elizabeth](https://goo.gl/maps/ZfbwsNaUjonKnoAY9) (Gqeberha) and [Durban](https://goo.gl/maps/C94hkSvFEopmUoJx9), respectively.
clues.summary: Metropolitan routes, big roads around cities, carry the letter M. The sign designs are distinct in one south-east port city and in the east coast city.

clues.title: Pole: three strips of reflective tape on signal poles
text: Traffic lights and pedestrian crossing poles in Johannesburg are encircled by three strips of **reflective tape**.

images.caption: A yellow signal pole with three strips of reflective tape

clues.summary: In the biggest northern city, traffic light and crossing poles have three strips of reflective tape around them.

clues.title: Street lamp: arm with a bump on top
text: While this lamp and arm can be found uncommonly across the country, Durban uniquely has this** bump** on the top. You may, however, still see the standard lamp and arm.

images.caption: A street lamp with an arm that has a bump on top, circled in red

clues.summary: This lamp and arm shows up rarely across the country, but one east coast city has a bump on top. You may still see the standard lamp.

clues.title: Poles: stuck-on adverts for abortion and enlargement pills
text: Poles or any public infrastructure will often be plastered with **dodgy adverts** for abortion services or penis enlargement pills in and around Gauteng, in particular in Johannesburg and Emalahleni.

images.caption: Poles covered in stuck-on adverts; a red circle and arrow zoom in on an advert on a pole, left

clues.summary: Poles and public property are often covered in dodgy adverts for abortion services or enlargement pills, in and around the northern urban area, especially the biggest city and one mining town.

clues.title: Road: reddish asphalt, dry grey trees, golden grass
text: The section of the **R360 north of Bokspits**, next to the Botswana border, has asphalt with a recognizable reddish tint. The landscape is arid and features dry greyish trees, shrubs and long golden grass. The road runs in a general north to south direction.
NOTE: Asphalt with a reddish tint can be found on other roads and the southern part of the R360. However, the landscape north of Bokspits looks predominantly like this.

images.caption: Road with reddish asphalt, dry grey trees and golden grass; the red circle zooms in on the road surface.

clues.summary: On one road north of a border village next to Botswana, reddish-tinted asphalt, arid land with grey dry trees, shrubs and long golden grass. The road runs north-south. Red asphalt also appears elsewhere, but this landscape is typical here.

clues.title: Landscape: flat-topped mountain with pyramid neighbour
text: The distinct **Table Mountain**, located west of Cape Town, can be recognized by its prominent three-kilometre plateau. It is flanked by Devil’s Peak, which is more pyramidal.
clues.summary: A famous mountain west of the main southern city with a 3 km flat plateau, flanked by a more pyramid-shaped peak.

clues.title: Landscape: mountains visible north of a southern city
text: Mountains in the Witfontein Nature Reserve, likely **George’s Peak**, will be visible **north** from the city of George.
clues.summary: Mountains in a nature reserve, likely a peak named after a man, are visible north of the southern coastal city.

clues.title: Google car: blue back means this country or Europe
text: If you see blue back of the google car with/or without antenna you can be only in South Africa or Europe.
With yellow outer lines and driving left you are gonna be only in South Africa.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A blue car back, with or without an antenna, means you are in this country or Europe. Add yellow edge lines and driving on the left, and it can only be here.

clues.title: Landscape: yellow boulders scattered around
text: In Limpopo, northeast of Polokwane, there are yellow boulders lying around as if a giant dropped his toys.

images.caption: Yellow boulders scattered around a field

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: In the north, north-east of the main city, big yellow boulders lie around as if a giant dropped his toys.

clues.title: Road lines: yellow edges, white centre vs Australia
text: In South Africa, most paved roads have **single yellow outer lines** and **white center lines**. This can be used to differentiate from Australia which has only **white lines** and never single yellow lines.
**REMEMBER:**
The Middle East can also have single yellow outer lines, so use driving side to tell them apart (South Africa drives left)
Botswana, Eswatini and Lesotho also use single yellow outer lines (but they usually have a white car)

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Most paved roads have single yellow edge lines and white centre lines. Australia only has white. Middle Eastern countries can have yellow edges too, so check driving side. Botswana, Eswatini and Lesotho share them but usually have a white car.

differs.how: Only white lines, never single yellow
